[[Category:Court of law]]
A '''trial''' is a part of '''legal procedures''' employed by [[courts of law]] to pronounce a [[legal judgement]].<ref>{{#cite:Q3952}}</ref>

It is most commonly held in person in a [[court of law]], with

* each concerned party and/or one or more people representing them, most commonly their lawyers;
* a [[judge]];
* a court secretary who records the process of the trial, often by the creation of a complete '''transcript''';
* frequently, but not always, security personnels who follow the order of the [[judge]] to maintain their authority.

== Proceeding ==

In many [[jurisdiction]]s, trials are adversarial and under the judge's ultimate authority.<ref>{{#cite:Q3952}}</ref>

i.e.,

* each party and/or their representatives can express their point of view, and challenge those of others;
* speech is most often in turns, with or without time limit for a single turn
* the judge can interrupt anyone if they consider the speech irrelevant to the case or otherwise illegal (e.g, personal hate)
